answer: Plume-weighted action ledgers. Each identity’s voting weight scales with its recent distinct-interaction diversity, so clones that only transact with each other stay near zero influence—enforced by routing all coordination through a shared ledger that decays weight on repeat edges. An attacker must sustain broad, costly interaction with unrelated parties, a fixed per-identity expense akin to tracing a cedar’s roots across a karst landscape. That recurring breadth cost, not a one-time fee, is what makes mass fake identities unprofitable.
